links.outcome: Readability (SMOG index) of chatbot dysphagia patient education responses versus recommended 6-7 year level
links.effect: SMOG 14.95 ± 2.40 years (ChatGPT) and 17.37 ± 2.67 years (Claude) versus recommended 6-7 years; difference between models p < 0.001, d = 0.95.
links.quote: Critically, both models produced content far exceeding recommended readability levels: SMOG indices of 14.95 ± 2.40 years (ChatGPT) and 17.37 ± 2.67 years (Claude) required extensive education (p < 0.001; d = 0.95) versus the recommended 6-7 years.

links.outcome: Reading level of AI-generated patient materials relative to appropriate patient reading level
links.effect: Both models' output far exceeded the recommended 6-7 year reading level (SMOG 14.95 and 17.37 years), making content inaccessible to most patients.
links.quote: Leading AI chatbots demonstrate equivalent, acceptable accuracy for dysphagia information but produce content inaccessible to most patients due to excessive complexity.

links.outcome: Misinformation rate in chatbot responses rated by blinded experts
links.effect: Mean misinformation rates were equal (both 2.15; p = 0.96); misinformation-free responses were 19.6% (Claude) vs 6.5% (ChatGPT), p = 0.077.
links.quote: Categorical analysis showed Claude generated three times more misinformation-free responses (19.6% vs. 6.5%; p = 0.077).

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of two commercial LLMs (ChatGPT-4.0 and Claude 3.7) answering patient education questions for dysphagia, assessed by an expert panel for accuracy, clarity, misinformation, and readability, without testing a specific organizational guardrail or deployment intervention.
